On this page

Bronze Medal Criterion #3

Make a useful contribution for future iGEM teams and document it on this page.

What iGEM asks for →

What we are contributing

Lead with the single most useful thing, then list the rest. Say who it is for and what it saves them.

Review · What we are contributing

Fix. This section was drafted overnight on 25 September from Measurement, Experiments, Hardware, Engineering and Parts, and nothing in it is new evidence. The team has to decide whether the measurement methods really are the headline contribution, since a judge will weigh that against the instruments. Check the four counts against their pages before the freeze: thirteen measurements, twenty-one protocols, sixteen protocol fix boxes and six cloning cycles. Add a sentence naming the person another team should contact, because Bronze criterion 3 is about a contribution somebody can actually pick up.

Hardware other teams can rebuild

The reactor, the photometer and the LED array as buildable objects: drawings, bill of materials, firmware, and the mistakes worth skipping. Link to the Hardware page rather than repeating it.

Review · Hardware other teams can rebuild

Fix. Drafted from the four instrument pages on 25 September; every figure here is quoted from them and none was checked against a file. Before the freeze somebody has to confirm what is actually downloadable, because the photometer page already carries an editorial note saying its release paragraph is not earned until the CAD, the bill of materials and the firmware are published with links; no firmware file is in this repository at all. Add the model numbers for the membrane and the pump to the Hardware pages rather than leaving them in the Results reference list. Price the two bills of materials, since a team choosing whether to rebuild decides on cost first. If the hydroponics models are not published, say so here.

Protocols and methods

Only protocols we actually ran and changed. A protocol copied out of a paper is not a contribution.

Review · Protocols and methods

Fix. Drafted on 25 September from Experiments and Measurement; the team must confirm that each of the six methods was in fact changed by the team rather than taken as written from a source, because a protocol copied out of a paper is not a contribution and a judge will ask. The SiO2 optical-density SOP is written and has never been run, so it is deliberately not in this table; decide whether to offer it as a method anyway and label it unrun. If the E8, E12 and E13 errors are corrected before the freeze, this section and the box above have to be updated on the same day.

Parts

If a part carries this criterion, the documentation must live on the Registry part page, not here. Link out and say what is there.

Where the documentation must live

If a part is used to fulfil this criterion, its documentation has to be on the part's entry in the Registry. This page points at it; it cannot stand in for it.

Review · Parts

Fix. This is the section that decides the criterion, and it cannot be finished from the wiki: somebody has to fill the eight Registry part pages and then list their numbers here. Decide which single part is offered for Bronze criterion 3 and write its Registry documentation first. Engineering says the part-by-part description of what each primer produced is on Parts, and Parts does not carry it; either write it there or point this page at Engineering. The Registry number column on Parts uses X for a part with no number yet, so nothing here should be published until those become real numbers.

How to reuse this

Concrete: clone this, print that, start here. Assume the reader has three weeks and no budget.

Review · How to reuse this

Fix. Drafted on 25 September from the pages linked in each step. Two of the five steps depend on files being downloadable, so check the model and firmware links before this list is published. Step 2 assumes a borrowed benchtop spectrophotometer; say what a team should do without one. If the team sets up a contact address or a repository for the models, put it at the top of this section, because a reuse instruction with no way to ask a question stops at the first problem.

The limits of what we are handing over

State what has not been validated, so nobody builds on a result we do not have.

Review · The limits of what we are handing over

Fix. Drafted on 25 September from the limitation statements already on Hardware, Results, Parts and Engineering. Keep this list even when the fixes close, and update each line on the day its fix closes, because a judge reads a limits section as a measure of how well a team knows its own work. Add the licence: the repository licence is CC BY 4.0 and the Software page describes the interface file as MIT, and a team cannot reuse a design whose licence is ambiguous.
